Post-mortem: Markdown export done

Shipped in one pull request inside the one-day appetite. One QA round and one review finding caught the same weak spot: file names.

Outcome

Done. Tested revision e21f8b6, PR #41. Delivered SC-1, SC-2 and SC-3.

Timeline

  1. build-P-1: serializer and file names, test first. S-1 green.
  2. build-P-2: menu item and Settings button. S-1 still green.
  3. QA round 1: J-1 and J-2 pass; J-3 fails, the zip makes a folder.
  4. Fix in 9c0a5f3; QA round 2: J-3 passes.
  5. PR #41 opened; end review raises F-1; fixed in e21f8b6.

Trace: trace page (fixture: no session captured).

How implementation went

P-1 · Serializer and export routes

Reused the owner check and the server's archive library. Created toMarkdown(), fileName() and two routes. Writing tests first made the checklist and link cases quick to get right.

P-2 · Download controls

Reused the existing menu item and button components. Plain links to the routes meant no download code in the browser.

Contributing factors

  • How did the zip get unsafe names? The zip route built entry names inline from the title instead of calling fileName(). The plan named the risk in "Look at these first", but no S-1 case tied the zip to the function until QA.
  • How did the header slip past QA? The QA titles were ASCII. "Q3/Q4 plans: draft?" tested unsafe characters, not non-ASCII ones.
  • How did it stay small? D-2 put all logic on the server, so the browser package had nothing to test beyond the journeys.

Surprises and deviations

OriginalActual
Checklists would export as writtenThe tick is a flag; the serializer writes "- [x]" itself
One file-name pathTwo paths until round 1; now one
One QA roundTwo of two used

Unexpected issues

A note title with a slash produced a file name the browser rewrote. Seen in QA round 1 on J-3; evidence in the verification page.

Critical decisions

Replace unsafe characters in file names with a hyphen rather than refusing the export. A routine technical choice inside P-1, so it was not relayed; recorded in the verification fix log.

Assumptions that were wrong

None.

Thrashing

None. J-3 failed once and passed after one fix.

Verification and review

J-1, J-2, J-3 and S-1 pass (verification). QA rounds: 2 of 2. Review points: the end review only, as planned. F-1 (Should-Fix, header for non-ASCII titles) fixed and closed (findings).

Lessons

  • When a plan says two paths must share one function, add a suite case that proves it before QA. Cost here: one QA round, about 20 minutes.
  • Seed test titles with non-ASCII characters whenever a title becomes a file name.
